slides.text: Me checking my seedlings <hl>14 times a day</hl> to see if anything happened.

slides.heading: Day 1: <hl>Nothing.</hl>
slides.body: You planted them this morning. You've looked four times. Still soil. This is normal. This is the whole first week.

slides.heading: Day 6: A tiny <hl>green loop</hl>
slides.body: Is that…? It is. You take a photo. You show someone who does not care as much as you do.

slides.heading: Day 9: They're all <hl>leaning</hl>
slides.body: They're reaching for the window. Turn the tray every day, or move them somewhere brighter. Tall and floppy means not enough light — not too much love.

slides.heading: Things That <hl>Actually Help</hl>
items: Check the soil, not the clock — water when the top is dry
A free class where you can ask the person who's done this a thousand times

slides.heading: Still Checking Every Hour? <hl>Same.</hl>
slides.body: Bring your seedling questions to our free, in-person class with Jason — every two weeks at Makerfarm in Alameda. Leave with a plan for your own space.

caption.instagram:
Me checking my seedlings 14 times a day to see if anything happened. 🌱

Nothing for a week is normal. Leaning means they want more light, not more water. Most seeds take 5–14 days, and most beginners find the waiting is the hard part.

Got a tray of seedlings and a lot of questions? Bring them to our free, in-person class with Jason — every two weeks at Makerfarm in Alameda. Register at the link in our bio.
